title: Performance Optimization Tips for CuTe DSL Kernels
critical_patterns: Identify bottlenecks using memory bandwidth, compute throughput, or latency.
Optimize occupancy by balancing active warps and resource allocation.
Coalesce memory access to improve bandwidth utilization.
Use shared memory for data reuse to reduce global memory access.
Leverage tensor cores for compute-intensive operations.
Minimize synchronization and use warp-level primitives when possible.
constraints: Threads per block should not exceed 1024.
Register usage should be balanced to avoid low occupancy.
Shared memory should be padded to avoid bank conflicts.
Block size should be a multiple of 32 for optimal occupancy.
Ensure problem size is large enough to amortize GPU launch overhead.
compressed_summary: This guide provides intermediate-level performance optimization techniques for CuTe DSL kernels, focusing on maximizing GPU efficiency. Key concepts include optimizing occupancy, memory bandwidth, and compute throughput while managing register pressure and instruction-level parallelism. Critical patterns involve identifying bottlenecks, optimizing occupancy by balancing active warps and resources, coalescing memory access, using shared memory for data reuse, leveraging tensor cores, and minimizing synchronization. Constraints include keeping threads per block under 1024, balancing register usage, padding shared memory to avoid bank conflicts, ensuring block size is a multiple of 32, and maintaining a large enough problem size to offset GPU launch overhead. Code snippets illustrate identifying bottlenecks, calculating occupancy, coalescing memory access, using tensor cores, and minimizing synchronization. The guide emphasizes profiling to identify real bottlenecks before optimizing, as the right optimization can lead to significant speedups. It provides a checklist for memory, compute, occupancy, launch configuration, and synchronization optimizations, and advises profiling as a first step before any optimization efforts.
